newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says Arabs should come to Sudan's aid.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says Arabs should come to Sudan's aid.

text.p: Jordan on Friday urged Arab states to come to Sudan's aid in its fight against secessionist rebels, saying the Khartoum government was facing a plot against its "territorial unity."

"What brotherly Sudan is being exposed to is a conspiracy aimed at the unity of its people and territory and this is a matter that necessitates from Arab countries a united stance," Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti was quoted as saying in remarks in local newspapers.

Kabariti said that this stance was ..."imperative to prevent the exploitation of Sudan's circumstances and to confront the enemies of the Arab nation to foil the possibility of harming Sudan's unity."
He did not elaborate on what support Arabs should give to Sudan's Islamist military government which has called for mobilisation against rebel assaults on eastern Sudan.

Rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) said on Friday in Eritrea that a joint rebel force was advancing on the key town of Damazin, which supplies Khartoum with most of its power, after seizing another town in the Blue Nile region.
There was no independent confirmation of the claim.

Sudan has accused Ethiopia and Eritrea of invading its territory and coordinating the rebel attacks. Both countries have denied involvement although Eritrea openly backs and houses Sudanese rebel groups.

Jordan's commercial and political ties with Sudan strengthened after Gulf donor states shunned the two countries for their support of Baghdad during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis sparked by Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
